verdict.rationale: Flagright ships its own rule engine. Rule instances can be created via the Management API as live entities that run checks on transactions, so rules fire automatically on transaction events, and a no-code rule builder and a Workflow Builder are also claimed. However, the evidence does not document which actions a rule hit triggers (blocking, auto-creating cases or alerts, status changes); only rule execution results are evidenced. Missing for 10: documented rule-to-action mapping (what happens when a rule fires), detail on Workflow Builder automation triggers, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: `POST /rule-instances` endpoint is used to create a new rule instance. A rule instance can be thought of as a live entity, that runs checks for for transactions.
